title: Federal and provincial funding cuts, 2024 borrowing by-laws
subtitle: Benchmarking report received, Community Justice Initiatives follow-up requested, and Reaching Home and children's services funding losses outlined.
overview: The committee heard a verbal update from the Commissioner of Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer on two funding reductions announced the previous week. Federal Reaching Home funding for homelessness, currently about $4.8 million a year, will be reduced for the next two fiscal years. The province is also ending its Transitional Grant for children's services in early 2024, leaving an estimated $2.1 million shortfall. Staff will bring options to the Budget Committee on December 13.

Through the consent agenda, the committee recommended that the Chief Financial Officer be authorized to borrow funds on a temporary basis in 2024 to meet operating and capital needs {{vote:m3}}. Council must still adopt this recommendation. The committee also received the 2022 MBNCanada performance report for information. It shows the Region scoring in the top or middle third on over three quarters of measures.

A councillor asked staff to report back on the status and impact of Community Justice Initiatives. These items matter to residents because the cuts affect housing, homelessness and child care services, and may shape the 2024 budget.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council authorize the Chief Financial Officer, by by-law, to borrow funds in 2024 on a temporary basis to meet operating and capital expenditure requirements.
The committee received the consent agenda items for information and approved them, including the 2023 property assessment growth report and the borrowing report.

debate: On the funding cuts, one councillor said the reductions underscore that the Region delivers essential services such as homelessness, housing and child care, yet may be seen as giving less service. The councillor argued that partnership with the provincial and federal governments is needed.

On the 2023 property assessment growth report, a councillor noted that expected revenue from aggregate operators being reclassified for tax purposes will not arrive until the assessment agency updates its system. The councillor stressed the money is not yet in hand.

On the MBNCanada report, staff said low cost per unit could show efficiency or underfunding, and high cost could reflect waste or simply the priority given to a service. Readers need to consider context.

One councillor noted the report places police staffing levels and per-capita police costs at the median among upper-tier comparators. Another cautioned that comparing municipalities is difficult because of differences in geography and in what residents want to fund.
